A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mixture of Concept Bottleneck Experts. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification and regression experiments, concept interventions, operator-vocabulary comparisons and ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds noisy-input intervention experiments in Appendix J.

M1.justification: The expression-tree mixture, selector, linear experts, training objectives and three-stage symbolic distillation procedure are retained. Expanded explanations of operator selection and one expression per expert do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The underlying datasets and tasks remain unchanged. Appendix J adds a strongly corrupted-input evaluation scenario for MNIST-Arithm, dSprites-Exp, Pendulum and MAWPS, extending coverage to a specific noisy deployment condition.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained experiments, including the KAN ablation. Figure 9 uses already evaluated methods: CEM, LICEM, MLP-M-CBE, Prior-M-CBE, Lin-M-CBE and Sym-M-CBE. Newly cited interpretable mixtures are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added Appendix J experiment specifies corruption as 0.5x + 0.5epsilon, with standard Gaussian epsilon, and sets expert counts to the known number of task mechanisms. This introduces a supplementary protocol; the retained Figure 6 still uses Pareto-knee configurations.

E4.justification: Appendix J and Figure 9 add a robustness test examining whether ground-truth concept interventions recover performance under strong input noise. This is a bounded extension of the existing intervention analysis; the KAN, concept-size and operator-vocabulary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals over five seeds. Figure 9 follows this existing practice, without introducing a different run-count policy, uncertainty estimator or significance test.

E6.justification: Tables 1–13 and the existing empirical plots retain their results. Figure 9 adds noisy-input intervention curves, including LICEM's approximately 100 MAE on MAWPS before intervention and stronger recovery by symbolic predictors. These are results under a newly reported condition, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The proof of Proposition 2, moved from Appendix B to C, corrects the grid-size substitution to h=(b-a)/M^(1/n), explicitly using M equal-measure cells over [a,b]^n instead of the inconsistent n_M/N expression. The proposition's approximation bound remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: controlling expert count and functional form, the Linear and Symbolic M-CBE instantiations, and their accuracy, interpretability and intervention benefits. The additional robustness evidence does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendices A and J add interpretations involving reasoning shortcuts and leakage-based robustness. Section 5.2 changes the proposed explanation for linear predictors' intervention responsiveness to alignment with the underlying task mapping. Section 5.3 drops the claim that vocabulary adaptation preserves performance; the stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a reproduction-code link, discloses the 0.9x + 0.1epsilon perturbation used in Section 5.2, and documents MAWPS filtering to four expression templates and numeric-value augmentation in Appendix K.2. These are added disclosures, without evidence that the retained experiments were rerun or their preparation changed.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds explicit comparisons with Pradier et al. (2021) and Ismail et al. (2022), alongside supporting citations elsewhere. It replaces the categorical single-equation and no-prior-concept-based-symbolic-regression assertions with positioning based on tabular versus raw inputs.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract and selected explanatory passages, moves leakage discussion into the preliminaries, and adds two appendices and acknowledgements. Author order, affiliation and publication text also change. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the four-panel Figure 9 with confidence bands and repositions existing material, notably Figure 5 and Table 2. Figures 1–8 retain their graphical content, while captions and surrounding page layout receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added noisy-input test supplies useful robustness evidence, while the corrected proof step, MAWPS and noise disclosures, and reproduction-code link improve clarity and reproducibility. Removing the performance-preserving adaptation claim also better matches Table 2. These are bounded gains: the method and primary results remain unchanged, and the new robustness evidence covers one Gaussian-corruption setting.
